title: Encoding of Sound Source Elevation in Human Cortex
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from two experiments investigating the cortical encoding of sound source elevation in humans. Subjects were presented with noise bursts from loudspeakers positioned at various elevations in a hemi-anechoic chamber, and were also tested on their ability to localize elevated sound sources. Experiment I used a deviant detection paradigm, while Experiment II used a one-back task involving sound elevation discrimination.
methods_description: Subjects underwent localization tests using pink noise bursts from loudspeakers at various elevations and a fixed azimuth. In Experiment I (deviant detection), subjects heard a long adapter noise from one loudspeaker followed by a short probe noise from another loudspeaker at different elevations, and behavioral responses to deviants were recorded. In Experiment II (one-back task), subjects heard white noise through open headphones followed by a noise burst from a loudspeaker at varying elevations, with occasional target trials requiring localization responses.
